value.rationale: The finite full-family cutoff covers all 2048 binary order-five universal cycles, a natural first sizeable odd-prime test of whether *every* de Bruijn sequence meets its sharp circular attractor lower bound. Counting all optimal sets reveals substantial nonrigidity (216 to 368 per cycle and 120 counts) not implied by the minimum itself, and supplies a reproducible benchmark for the open general behavior. A complete natural finite classification can be valuable without an all-order theorem; not an arbitrary hand-picked slice.
